centralQuestion: How can light reveal an obstacle without being absorbed or reflected by it?
thesis: In an ideal aligned interferometer, an absorbing obstacle changes interference and allows a previously dark detector to click without absorbing that detected photon; other trials can fail.
viewerPayoff: The click reveals a blocked possibility without absorption of the detected photon, while unsuccessful trials retain risk.

sources.organization: Elitzur and Vaidman / Tel Aviv University; Foundations of Physics
sources.title: Quantum Mechanical Interaction-Free Measurements (1993)
sources.notes: Theory and ideal apparatus; real alignment, leakage and detector noise matter. No preferred path or interpretation asserted. No general zero disturbance claim.

sources.organization: Kwiat, Weinfurter and Zeilinger / Scientific American; author-hosted Illinois copy
sources.title: Quantum Seeing in the Dark (November 1996)
sources.notes: Participant explanation, not independent replication or raw data review. Production uses an ideal Mach-Zehnder absorbing-obstacle model, not a replica of their Michelson mirror experiment. 1995 PRL researcher PDF was image-only: fetched and attempted text extraction, but body not inspected; not used as verified evidence.
